actions.action: Inspect black dots on stems with a magnifier and try scraping them off
Cut away black, mushy or hollow roots and soft or dark stem sections
Rinse the cutting in lukewarm water
Optionally dip cut ends in hydrogen peroxide or diluted cinnamon
Restart the cutting in a clean jar with only the nodes submerged
Do full water changes every 3–7 days instead of topping off
Let tap water sit out before use
If it doesn't recover, plant the healthiest node in a perlite/peat mix or LECA
If potted, keep moist by watering from below
Place the plant in bright, indirect light

reason: The answer correctly identifies root rot from topped-off, oxygen-poor water as the main cause and advises trimming, rinsing and full water changes, but it omits the fertilizer and container-size parts of the fix, and nothing it suggests is harmful.
